panels.figure_caption: Ancient, crowded infestations. (a) From sample Chi-8-Nit (∼300 BP), a textile made of human hair; (b) hair from the mummy sample SJArg-4-Nit. Both panels show chains of Nits along the same hair shaft, equating to nit clusters, which are markers of severe infestations.
in_text_mentions: bric, P. humanus humanus. Lice can produce supernumerary infestations (Alexander 1984; Lambiase and Perotti 2019), characterized by the occurrence of a large number of nits (lice eggs) homogeneously distributed on head hairs and, especially concentrated on the hair shaft toward the root end (Lambiase and Perotti 2019). Crowded infestations have frequently been recorded from ancient human mummies, with great numbers of nits attached not only to hair (see fig. 1) but to their clothing as well (Araujo et al. 2000; Reinhard and Buikstra 2003; Arriaza et al. 2012; Dutra et al. 2014; Lynnerup 2015).

brown (viable) and translucent (empty) nits seen on polarized dermoscopy

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photo of real patient facial hair with yellowish deposits corresponding to nits, with diagnosis of phthiriasis (pubic lice in facial hair) supported by caption and in-text mentions. B: Polarized dermoscopy showing crab-shaped parasites with broad bodies and thick claws clutching hair shafts plus viable and empty nits, diagnostic of Phthirus pubis infestation in ectopic facial hair site.
panels.attribution_text: Jayasree et al. Pubic Lice in Facial Hair.. Dermatology practical & conceptual 2020. doi:10.5826/dpc.1002a42. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: (A) Facial hair showing yellowish deposits and erythema of underlying skin. (B) Crab- shaped pubic lice with thick claws grasping hair shafts along with brown (viable) and translucent (empty) nits seen on polarized dermoscopy.
in_text_mentions: ct with a female acquaintance 3 days prior to the onset of symptoms. Examination revealed yellowish deposits on the moustache and facial hair below the lower lip with erythema of the underlying skin (Figure 1A). On dermoscopy, crab-shaped parasites with broad bodies and thick claws were spotted clutching the hair shafts. Viable nits containing unhatched nymphs and empty translucent nit casings were also seen attached to proximal hair shafts (Figure 1B). Examination of the remaining hair-bearing skin including pubic area and eyelashes did not yield any findings. Thus a diagnosis of phthiriasis

panels.figure_caption: An array of lice eggs attached to the shafts of pubic hairs under direct microscopic examination (magnification ×40). This figure appears in color at www.ajtmh.org.
in_text_mentions: clinic with a 6-month history of severe itching in the inguinal area on February 25, 2022. This patient worked at a construction site and reported that he had had no recent sexual contact. He had treated himself with diesel oil, but there was no improvement in his condition. Physical examination was notable for multiple black dots on the base of the pubic hair shaft and whitish-appearing concretions attached to the shafts of pubic hairs (Figure 1), microscopic examination of the hair sample showed an array of insect eggs like silkworm chrysalis attached to the shafts of pubic hairs (Figure 2).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Panel A shows upper lid eyelashes with multiple nits and adult lice, captioned as Phthirus pubis phthiriasis palpebrarum. B: Panel B shows upper lid eyelashes with multiple nits and adult lice, same manifestation as panel A per caption. C: Panel C shows lower lid eyelashes with nits/lice and dried blood on skin, captioned lower lid infestation.

in_text_mentions: e adult P. pubis firmly attached to the base and shaft of eyelashes. Lid margin vascular engorgement and mild hyperemia were observed in the conjunctiva. There was mild punctate defect on corneal epithelium. No nit, lice or any abnormal of ocular surface were observed in the left eye. The left cornea was clear and no vision decline.
